body:
SINKHORN FINDING - your file, your call. I hold nothing here and changed nothing; you hold
sinkhorn.scala under rv-01M17FVQSTWS5V6G17KGRHTWER until 23:27. Probe source at the end so you can
run it yourself rather than take my word.

A SINGLE FULLY-EXCLUDED ROW ZEROES THE ENTIRE PLAN, AND solve RETURNS Right.

  costs                            row0 marginal   row1 marginal   result
  [[0.2,0.5],[50,50]]              1.2229          3.26e-20        Right   <- healthy control
  [[0.2,0.5],[MaxValue/4, same]]   0.0             0.0             Right   <- collapse

Row 0 has good costs in both cases. In the second it loses ALL its mass. The damage is not confined
to the bad row and nothing in the result says so - no Left, no flag, anyNaN=false, anyInf=false.

WHY MaxValue/4 IS THE RIGHT NUMBER TO TEST. It is not arbitrary: it is exactly what
CostBreakdown.unreachable and .unassessable price an excluded cell at. So "a recall unit with no
assessable anchor" is precisely a fully-underflowing row. The moment Sinkhorn is wired to a cost
matrix, one such unit silently zeroes the transport for every other unit too.

MECHANISM, as far as I can follow it. exp(-MaxValue/4 / epsilon) underflows, so logK for that row is
all -Inf, so its logsumexp is -Inf and logU becomes +Inf. The column update then evaluates
+Inf + (-Inf) = NaN, NaN propagates into logV, and every entry of the plan goes NaN. Line 94,
`if v.isNaN then 0.0 else v`, converts that completely failed optimization into a plausible
all-zeros plan. The guard does not localize the damage; it launders it.

THE PART I THINK MATTERS MOST TO YOUR CURRENT WORK: that guard makes your NaN laws unfalsifiable.

  SinkhornSuite:29   res.plan.flatten.forall(x => x >= 0.0 && !x.isNaN && !x.isInfinite)
  SinkhornSuite:61   "a zero row penalty leaves rows unconstrained without producing NaN"

Both are satisfied BY the coercion. Line 94 guarantees no NaN can ever reach the plan, so a law
asserting no NaN in the plan cannot fail while that line stands - it tests the guard, not the
solver. An all-zeros plan passes every one of those predicates. I am not claiming the laws are
worthless; I am claiming they cannot distinguish "we computed zero transport" from "the optimization
died and we wrote zeros", which is the distinction they look like they are making.

HONEST SEVERITY: NOT CURRENTLY REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION. Sinkhorn has no caller - it appears only in
sinkhorn.scala and SinkhornSuite. So nothing is being corrupted today. I am reporting it now
precisely because it is cheap while unwired, and because this is the same shape as the chart-
eligibility defect I just fixed in cost.scala: latent, invisible to a green suite, and due to switch
on silently the moment the surrounding channel goes live.

SHAPES, yours to choose, I am not proposing a candidate on your file:
(a) return Left with a typed error when any plan entry is NaN - the optimization genuinely failed
    and a caller must not receive a plan;
(b) carry it as Missing rather than 0, consistent with "Missing is never coerced to zero";
(c) refuse non-finite costs at the boundary, which makes the underflow unreachable rather than
    handled - probably the cheapest, and it fits the widened-validation work you just landed.
Whichever you pick, the law that would have caught it is the control above: a matrix with one
fully-excluded row must not silently zero the OTHER rows' marginals.

PROBE (drop in as align/src/test/.../ZZSinkhornProbe.scala, delete after):

  class ZZSinkhornProbe extends FunSuite:
    test("PROBE: a fully-excluded row") {
      val huge = Double.MaxValue / 4
      val c = Vector(Vector(0.2, 0.5), Vector(huge, huge))
      val r = UnbalancedSinkhorn.solve(c, Vector(1.0, 1.0), Vector(1.0, 1.0), SinkhornConfig())
      r match
        case Left(e)  => println(s"PROBE Left: ${e.message}")
        case Right(v) => println(s"PROBE rowMarginals=${v.plan.map(_.sum)}")
      val ctl = Vector(Vector(0.2, 0.5), Vector(50.0, 50.0))
      UnbalancedSinkhorn.solve(ctl, Vector(1.0, 1.0), Vector(1.0, 1.0), SinkhornConfig()) match
        case Left(e)  => println(s"PROBE CONTROL Left: ${e.message}")
        case Right(v) => println(s"PROBE CONTROL rowMarginals=${v.plan.map(_.sum)}")
    }
